reason:
Passes the feasibility/schedule lens, with conditions. It is a one-value change of an env knob that already exists (BIOHUB_REPAIR_DEADLINE_S, checked per dataset against KERNEL_START_TS set in cell 0). The degraded path it moves was already run by the FD dummy (DEADLINE at 975 s, safetail keeps safe divisions + linefit, 28.1 s/clip mean, 45.6 s max). So the output is byte-identical whenever the deadline does not fire, and the fallback is the same fail-soft path. The K3 dummy gates it through its SAFETAIL log line, and it rides K3 in S4 (26.09 ~10-13 UTC) with no extra slot, well before the 27.09 12:00 R8 cutoff. The builder and test edit is ~0.5 h (build_probe_kernel.py l.1849; tests/test_safetail.py l.153-183 already hold the refusal cases). In the normal world (s~1, N<=97 from L35<=7.73 h) it adds 0 s of hidden-run time. Caveats found:
(1) 'Runtime cost 0 s' holds only when nothing fires. In slow worlds it spends up to ~1 h of the remaining headroom and opens narrow timeout bands where 9.5 h would have finished degraded. Step-0 model + 8 h insertion gate: N=106 at s~2.08-2.13 (11.74 h vs 12.02 h); N=130 at s~1.72-1.88. In the N~199 world (hidden hardware faster for #34/#35), a later run at dummy speed would time out at s>=~1.08 instead of ~1.15. All of these worlds are improbable, and a timeout shows up as an error on the public LB, since public+private run in one pass. It is never a silent private loss.
(2) The why_now arithmetic is overstated. At 1.25x the model gives 9.3-9.8 h with 0-15 degraded clips, not 10.65 h with 26. The benefit starts at s~1.4-1.5.
(3) The admissibility gain is mostly moot. R5(b) already admits a 9.5-10.5 h latency when the step-0 forecast (~7.9 h) clears 9.5 h by >=1 h.
(4) It rewrites binding pre-registered numbers: R5(a) 9.5 h, the F2 condition 'latency of F1 <= 9.5 h', and the S10-S11 trigger. The pre-registration says 'apply mechanically, do not rewrite', so it needs an explicit user OK. It is not covered by the standing rider OK.
(5) The sha256-twin gate (K3 built with 34200) costs an extra dummy (~0.5 GPU-h from the 11 h quota shared with the exp60 lab). It is redundant, because the value only enters a comparison that never fires on a ~1,500 s dummy.
(6) The ledger clause 'shift DIVINS_DEADLINE_S by the same delta' contradicts the idea's own advice not to move DIVINS later.
(7) Confound: if K2 degrades at 9.5 h in a slow world and K3 does not, the K3-K2 delta includes the deadline gain and could wrongly admit forkmid under R4.
fix: Adopt only in this reduced form. (a) Get the user's explicit OK to change 9.5 h to 10.5 h in R5(a), the F2 latency condition and the S10-S11 trigger, for builds that carry 37800 only. (b) Whitelist exactly {34200, 37800} without --lab and add test cases: 37800 is accepted and writes os.environ BIOHUB_REPAIR_DEADLINE_S='37800' in cell 0; 36000 and 1 are refused without --lab. (c) Gate: the K3 dummy log must show 'SAFETAIL: repair deadline 37800s, divins deadline 28800s', and a probe.json diff against the K3 plan may differ only in REPAIR_DEADLINE_S. Drop the sha twin dummy (no extra GPU). (d) Activate only if the observed L(K2) <= 8.5 h. Otherwise keep 34200, because a slow K2 means the timeout bands are reachable. (e) Keep DIVINS_DEADLINE_S at 28800 and drop the ledger clause that shifts it. The ledger shrinks to one line per rider: its dummy repair s/clip vs K2. (f) If L(K2) or L(K3) falls in 9.5-10.5 h, do not use K3-K2 as an R4 delta for forkmid without noting the deadline confound.
realistic_gain: About 0 in the expected world. It only matters when a K3/F1 run is >=1.4x slower than #35 (P ~0.01-0.03, given dummy GPU spread of ~+-12% and GPU ~55% of runtime). There it saves ~10-30 degraded clips, worth ~+0.002-0.008. E ~ +0.0001 private, offset by a smaller timeout-band risk of the same order. The cost is 0.5 agent-h, no LB slot and no GPU if the sha twin is dropped.
